deliverable: claude-code-harness v1.19.2-v1.19.4 (commits a95dade..3ff5002) - documented WebSearch x effort behaviour
summary: All four claims (A-D) re-derived from scratch on an independently built harness. 14 headless child sessions, n>=2 per row, zero reuse of the authoring session's artifacts. Every row carries a WebSearch-invocation control; every failing row states its own effort tier via the API rejection text. No published number failed to reproduce.

environment.note: No CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL anywhere in settings or environment, so the --effort flag is the top-ranked mechanism in every run below. Parent-injected vars were stripped per run (see unset_list).

method.unset_list: env -u CLAUDE_EFFORT -u CLAUDECODE -u CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID -u CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION -u CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT -u CLAUDE_CODE_SSE_PORT -u CLAUDE_CODE_TASK_LIST_ID -u CLAUDE_PID -u CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL -u AI_AGENT
method.session_command_template: cd <scratch>/sandbox && env -u ... claude -p "$(cat prompt-session.txt)" --model <MODEL> --effort <TIER> --output-format stream-json --verbose </dev/null > runs/<TAG>.jsonl
method.agent_command_template: cd <scratch>/sandbox && env -u ... claude -p "Delegate with the Task tool to the subagent type \`<AGENT>\`. The task you give it, verbatim: 'Search the web with the query: Anthropic Claude model release notes'. When it returns, reply with its exact one-line report and nothing else. Do NOT call WebSearch yourself under any circumstances." --model claude-opus-5 --effort xhigh --output-format stream-json --verbose </dev/null > runs/<TAG>.jsonl
method.session_prompt:
Do exactly two things, in this order, then stop:
1. Run the Bash command: printenv CLAUDE_EFFORT
2. Call the WebSearch tool exactly once with the query: Anthropic Claude model release notes
Then reply with a single line: DONE
Do not use any other tools. Do not retry WebSearch if it fails - report and stop.

oracles.name: failure_oracle_self_stating
oracles.cmd: grep -c "is not supported when thinking is disabled" <run>.jsonl ; grep -o "output_config.effort '[a-z]*'" <run>.jsonl | sort -u
oracles.why: The API rejection names the tier it rejected, so a failing run states its own effort without presupposing the claim.

oracles.name: invocation_control
oracles.why: A zero-error run proves nothing unless the tool was actually called. Every pass row below has count >= 1.

oracles.name: model_control
oracles.why: Confirms the --model flag took effect rather than assuming it.

oracles.name: level_readback_corroborating
oracles.why: Session rows run `printenv CLAUDE_EFFORT` inside the child. Secondary, not load-bearing: the differential between the high and xhigh rows (identical commands but for the flag value) is what proves the flag took hold.

oracles.name: result_substance
oracles.cmd: grep -o 'Web search results for query[^,]*' / grep -c 'https://' over tool_result bodies
oracles.why: Distinguishes a real search from an empty or silently-degraded one.

method.positive_control: runs/pilot-high.jsonl and runs/opus-high-2.jsonl were expected to PASS and did - WebSearch invoked, 0 rejections, real link lists returned. The harness therefore demonstrably separates success from failure.

raw_results.notes: returned link list incl. support.claude.com, platform.claude.com; final text 'DONE' + Sources
real 'Web search results for query' body with links
real 'Web search results for query' body with links

claims.claim: On session model claude-opus-5, WebSearch fails at effort xhigh and succeeds at high.
claims.published_in: CHANGELOG 1.19.2; native-capabilities.md Effort table rows 'high --effort high: ok 0/2' and 'xhigh --effort xhigh: fails 3/3'

observed.opus5_high: 2/2 pass - websearch_tool_use=1 each, effort_400_hits=0 each, real link lists returned, CLAUDE_EFFORT read back 'high'
observed.opus5_xhigh: 2/2 fail - websearch_tool_use=1 each, effort_400_hits=3 each, every rejection quotes output_config.effort 'xhigh', CLAUDE_EFFORT read back 'xhigh'

claims.discrepancy_vs_published: none. Published table gives failure ratios per mechanism (3/3, 4/4, 3/3, 2/2); my n=2 at --effort xhigh reproduces the same direction and the same quoted tier. Per-run rejection count differs (3 here vs 'two per run' stated in the doc) - a retry-count artefact of prompt shape, not of the claim.

claims.claim: On session models claude-sonnet-5 and claude-fable-5, WebSearch succeeds at xhigh.
claims.published_in: CHANGELOG 1.19.3 'The ceiling is Opus 5's, not Claude Code's - 0/8 failures'; native-capabilities.md 'Which model is affected'

observed.sonnet5_xhigh: 2/2 pass - websearch_tool_use=1, effort_400_hits=0, real 'Web search results for query' bodies with links, model_observed claude-sonnet-5, CLAUDE_EFFORT 'xhigh'
observed.fable5_xhigh: 2/2 pass - websearch_tool_use=1, effort_400_hits=0, real results, model_observed claude-fable-5, CLAUDE_EFFORT 'xhigh'

claims.discrepancy_vs_published: none for xhigh. Scope note: the published 0/8 spans xhigh AND max for both models; I re-derived xhigh only (4 of those 8 cells). The max cells were not re-tested and are neither confirmed nor refuted here.

claims.claim: A subagent defined in .claude/agents/*.md with effort: high can use WebSearch even when the session is claude-opus-5 at xhigh; the same agent with no effort: declared cannot.
claims.published_in: CHANGELOG 1.19.4 Fixed ('effort: high searched 2/2 with no 400, an agent declaring nothing failed 2/2'); 1.19.3; native-capabilities.md delegate table; harness-discipline.md Subagents spawn rule

observed.effort_high_agent: 2/2 pass - delegate returned 'SEARCH_OK 6 links' both runs; websearch_tool_use=1 with a non-null parent_tool_use_id, confirming the call fired inside the delegate; effort_400_hits=0
observed.no_effort_agent: 2/2 fail - delegate returned SEARCH_FAIL carrying the verbatim 400; effort_400_hits=5 per run; every rejection quotes 'xhigh', which is the session's level and therefore direct evidence of inheritance

claims.isolation: wsr-high.md and wsr-plain.md differ only in the `effort: high` line (plus name/description). diff output recorded in run log.
claims.session_level_control: Not assumed. The wsr-plain rejection text names 'xhigh' - the session tier - which both confirms the session was at xhigh and demonstrates the delegate inherited it. Independently, rows opus-xh-1/2 show --effort xhigh takes hold on this machine (CLAUDE_EFFORT readback 'xhigh').
claims.discrepancy_vs_published: none. This is the exact load path v1.19.4 says it re-verified (.claude/agents/*.md YAML frontmatter, not --agents), and it reproduces at the published 2/2 - 2/2.

claims.claim: Declaring tools: without WebSearch removes the tool entirely - the delegate reports having none rather than erroring.
claims.published_in: CHANGELOG 1.19.3 Added ('a narrowed allowlist drops it outright, and the delegate reports having no such tool rather than erroring'); native-capabilities.md delegate table row 'tools: narrowed, WebSearch omitted - tool absent, never called'; harness-discipline.md
claims.observed: 2/2 - websearch_tool_use=0 (tool never invoked), effort_400_hits=0 (no error of any kind), delegate's final report 'NO_SUCH_TOOL' both runs. Notably the delegate could not reach WebSearch via ToolSearch either, though ToolSearch is how the unrestricted delegate loaded it in ag-high-1.
claims.method_note: My wsr-notools declares `effort: high` alongside the narrowed `tools:`. That is a stronger isolation than the published row, which ran the narrowed agent on claude-sonnet-5: here the effort tier would have permitted search, so the only thing that can explain the absence is the allowlist.
claims.discrepancy_vs_published: none on the claim. Method differs from the published row's model pin (opus-5/effort high here vs sonnet-5 there); outcome identical.

residual_gaps: max tier for sonnet-5/fable-5 (4 of the published 8 cells in claim B) not re-tested.
CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL env-layer rows from the published tables were out of scope for this mandate and were not re-derived.
The published `effort: xhigh` delegate row and the `model: claude-sonnet-5` delegate rows were out of scope and not re-derived.
n=2 per row. Direction is unambiguous (0/6 pass rows produced a rejection; 4/4 fail rows produced one naming the correct tier), but these are not tight rate estimates.
